prompt: A candy company claims its five colors are produced in equal proportions. A student counts the colors in a large bag and runs a chi-square goodness-of-fit test. How many degrees of freedom does the test have?
hint: Degrees of freedom in a goodness-of-fit test depend on how many categories there are, not on how many candies were counted.

hints.text: Degrees of freedom in a goodness-of-fit test depend on how many categories there are, not on how many candies were counted.
The rule is the number of categories minus $1$. There are five colors, so subtract $1$ from $5$.
$5 - 1 = 4$, so the test has $4$ degrees of freedom.

explanation: A goodness-of-fit test has one category for each possible outcome, which here means the 5 colors.
Once four category counts are known the fifth is fixed by the total, so the degrees of freedom are $k - 1 = 5 - 1$.
The test has $4$ degrees of freedom. (The number of candies in the bag does not affect this.)

alternativeExplanations.title: Why minus one
steps: Once you know the total and four of the five counts, the fifth count is forced.
Only four counts are "free" to vary.
